text:
Maya Chen: Heads up, we're seeing a P95 latency spike on model-prod v2 around 09:23 UTC. P95 jumped from ~12ms to ~75ms for short-seq (<=64). Throughput dropped ~18%. Rolling windows show it started around 1895012300 and cleared around 1895012440.

Jonah Patel: Which GPU type / instance? Any kernel-autoselector logs? :thinking_face:

Maya Chen: A100-SXM4 nodes, auto-selector logs attached (snippet):
```
[selector] model=llama-13b-v2 seq=32 chosen_kernel=gemm_sparse_fallback reason=workspace_exceeded workspace_needed=420MiB workspace_limit=384MiB
[selector] reroute=enabled fallback_to=sgemms path=gemm_path
```
Also nvprof counters show tensorcore_kernels=0, sgemm_launches=7 for the hot request batch.

Alejandra Ruiz: workspace_exceeded is interesting — but earlier today I saw kernel selection flip when PCIe throughput saturated (kernel prefers tensorcore path but falls back on constrained interconnect). Could be noisy neighbor saturating PCIe/NVLINK.

perf-bot: Automated alert: gpu-node-12 pci_read_bw spike detected at 09:22:58 UTC. rx=9.6GB/s (baseline 3.4GB/s). top-ten processes by PCIe: vm-guest-7 (QEMU) dominated.

Ryan O'Neill: dmesg had repeated warnings around the same time about BAR2 remap retries on gpu2, plus host-level NIC bursts from a tenant VM. Sounds like host-level contention.

Jonah Patel: Can you paste the selector debug dump and a short tracelog from the runtime? Also run `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` and capture `nv-hostengine` metrics for the window.

Maya Chen: Posted a compact trace:
```
[09:22:50] request id=... latency_start
[09:22:51] selector: evaluated 6 kernels -> pref=tensorcore_gemm workspace=278MiB
[09:22:51] pci_read_bw=8.9GB/s -> decision: fall back to gemm_path
[09:22:51] launch sgemm kernel (no tc) -> p99/k=74ms
```
Also attached `nvidia-smi pmon` snapshot showing SM util dropped from 78% -> 41% when fallback happened.

Alejandra Ruiz: That matches a scenario where the runtime chooses a kernel that avoids extra workspace or scratch allocation because PCIe pressure increases transfer latency for the tiled tensorcore path. The selector currently assumes workspace allocation cost only, but it doesn't account for dynamic interconnect bandwidth.

Ryan O'Neill: Quick mitigation idea: we can force the selector to prefer tensorcore kernels for this model temporarily with env flag `RR_FORCE_TENSORCORES=true` in the pod config to see if latency returns to normal (may increase workspace usage). Anyone object to a small canary? :rocket:

Jonah Patel: Do it on a single canary host first. Also capture perf counters (sm_eff, inst_executed, dram_read_bytes) to compare.

Maya Chen: Canary applied to two hosts at 09:35. Results: P95 dropped back to ~14ms on canary, throughput for canary dropped 8% due to extra workspace copies and slightly higher memory ops. Non-canary remained high.

perf-bot: Canary report: canary-hosts avg_p95=14ms, baseline-hosts avg_p95=72ms, canary_throughput=-8% vs baseline.

Alejandra Ruiz: So forcing tensorcores helps latency but costs throughput — expected tradeoff. We should root-cause the PCIe saturation. If it's noisy neighbor VM-guest-7 we can ask infra to migrate or throttle. Also runtime can be improved: incorporate a dynamic interconnect penalty into the kernel scoring function.

Ryan O'Neill: Filed infra ticket INFRA-2219 to evict/inspect VM-guest-7 and check host oversubscription. Assigned to @infra oncall.

Maya Chen: For completeness I also captured a Triton selector trace: it logged workspace_probe_timeout=250ms in one case which triggered fallback. Might be due to delayed allocation because hypervisor preemption.

Jonah Patel: Long-term fixes: (1) extend selector cost model to include measured PCIe/NVLINK bandwidth and/or allocation latency; (2) add grace period before switching kernels for short sequences; (3) emit selector telemetry so we can correlate with PCIe counters automatically.

Alejandra Ruiz: I can prototype a bandwidth-aware penalty term in the selector this week. Will add a config knob `selector.bandwidth_penalty` default=0.

Ryan O'Neill: Short-term: keep `RR_FORCE_TENSORCORES=true` on critical capacity for a few hours while infra mitigates noisy tenant. Also add an alert that fires when selector fallback_rate > 5% and pci_rx_bw > 7GB/s.

Maya Chen: Incident created: incident/1895012345-noisy-pcie-kernel-fallback. I'll add collected traces, nvprof snapshots, and the canary results. Follow-up: postmortem with timeline and selector change proposal.

Jonah Patel: Thanks team. Action items: Alejandra prototype selector change, Infra to investigate VM, Ops to keep canary flag until infra resolves.

Maya Chen: Closing thread for now — will update incident doc when infra confirms eviction. :white_check_mark:
